newsitem.title: DUBAI: HORSE RACING-NO CIGAR FOR WORLD'S RICHEST RACE.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-NO CIGAR FOR WORLD'S RICHEST RACE.

text.p: The hype for the world's richest horse race has begun but this time there is no Cigar.
The all-conquering American wonder horse which triumphed over 2,000 metres of desert sand in the inaugural running of the $4 million Dubai World Cup last year has subsequently retired.
"There won't be that fairy tale this year," the race committee's Irish chairman Michael Osborne said on Wednesday.
"There isn't another horse like Cigar," he said at Dubai's Nad al-Sheba dirt track.

Cigar, an imposing six-year-old colt owned by U.S. aviation tycoon Allen Paulson and trained by Bill Mott, finished half a length ahead of composer Burt Bacharach's Soul of the Matter with L'Carriere, the third American thoroughbred in the field of 11, eight lengths behind.
Osborne said U.S. horses were unlikely the dominate this year's event, a championship for older middle-distance horses.
Some 94 horses have been nominated for the March 29 race, which is worth $2.4 million to the winner and is billed as racing's heavyweight title.

The event has been switched to a Saturday from Wednesday to allow more television viewers around the world to watch the race, which will be run under floodlights. Last year's event was relayed to television stations in 150 countries.
The deadline for further entries is February 5 and the field of 14 runners selected from all continents will be announced on February 12.
Helissio, winner of the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe in October, Bijou d'Inde and Timarida, lead the line-up. Preakness Stakes champion Louis Quatorze heads 33 North American entries.
The event is the brainchild of Dubai's Crown Prince Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid al-Maktoum, the world's most successful racehorse owner and breeder.
Organisers hope it will reinforce Dubai's image as a modern trade and tourism centre and the Middle East's sporting capital.

"Cigar winning last year helped enormously, as you can't beat a world champion who's just won 14 races in a row for dazzling publicity," said Kevin Greely, Dubai World Cup's Kentucky-born racing secretary.
